## What this letter says
This letter gives the results of a scan of your left knee (MRI). An MRI is a scan that uses magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body.

- There may be a small tear in your knee. It is at the back part of the inner cartilage (medial meniscus). This is not certain. A tear cannot be ruled out.
- There is no broken bone.
- A ligament inside your knee is intact. It is called the ACL (anterior cruciate ligament).
- There is mild, early wear and tear (osteoarthritis). It is on the inner side of your knee.
- There is a little fluid in your knee.
- Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do
1. Go to physiotherapy for 6 to 8 weeks. Your doctor has sent you there.
2. Go back to the orthopaedic clinic in 3 months. The doctor will see you again.
3. You can carry on with normal activities, as far as pain allows.

## Dates and medicines
- 1 September 2026: you had the MRI scan of your left knee.
- Physiotherapy: for 6 to 8 weeks.
- Orthopaedic clinic visit: in 3 months. The letter does not give an exact date.
- Medicines: the letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What will happen at physiotherapy, and when does it start?
- How will I get the date for my clinic visit in 3 months?
- What do the words "medial meniscus" and "osteoarthritis" mean?
- What does it mean that a tear cannot be ruled out?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
